mode_evidence: Signs are said to be 'seen' (a pale, murky vapor, your own skull, a bright white nimitta) and mastery gives 'the ability to see without opening your eyes', but the glossary calls nimitta a 'mental sign or image' and Lee also says they can be made small, large, near, far 'through the power of thought', which leans imaginal. The digest does not settle whether the white light is a visual-field percept.
onset_evidence: Method 1 is an induction of sorts: move the mind through bases in the head (forehead, top of head, middle of brain), spread the refined breath, and 'you may find' signs arise. For someone who sees nothing the foreword says signs are individual, 'not really essential', and should not be forced; if none come, 'learn how to use what you do experience'. No time scale in the digest.

conditions.prerequisites: Mind and breath put in order and made stable before receiving 'guests'; mastery of the seven basic steps.
conditions.other: Study with a skilled teacher recommended for the knowledge-use stage.

stages.label: signs (nimitta)
stages.description: Arise once breath spreads through the head: tingling, pale murky vapor, own skull.

stages.label: bright white nimitta
stages.description: Chosen, enlarged to head size, lowered to centre of chest, spread to every pore; body parts may appear as pictures.

stages.label: mastery
stages.description: Brilliantly white ball or lump of light can be produced at will and used as a field for knowledge or mental pictures.

what_to_do_with_light: Take only one sign at a time, enlarge it to head size, bring it to the chest, spread it with the breath through the body; later evoke at will. Unwanted signs: long deep breaths into the heart dismiss them. Do not be pleased or upset by whatever appears.
obstacles_and_fixes: Unwanted nimitta: breathe deep and long down into the heart.
Unwanted body pictures: take two or three long breaths.
Signs you cannot control: have nothing to do with them.
cautions: Getting hooked on visions breeds pride and strays from the Middle Path.
Treat visions as arising, fading and disappearing; stay neutral.
interpretation: The white nimitta is a pure breath that can cleanse the blood and ease pain; signs are 'guests' of the breath, and the glossary calls them mental sign or image.
practice_summary: Settle on the breath and shift awareness through bases in the head, letting each spot fill with refined breath and spread downward. Keep awareness broad. When signs appear (tingling, a pale murky vapor, your skull) do not be moved by them; if you do not want them, breathe long and deep into the heart. If one appears that you want, take it one at a time, expand it to the size of your head, bring it down to the centre of the chest, make the breath and light as white and bright as possible, and let both spread to every pore. Keep the mind on the refined breath alone. With practice you can raise the white ball of light at will and use it as a field for knowledge. If no signs come, they are not essential; do not force.

key_passages.anchor: Signs and visions, for example: Some people experience them, others
key_passages.paraphrase: Signs and visions are individual and not essential; if they do not come, use what does.

key_passages.anchor: you may find that the breath starts giving rise to various signs
key_passages.paraphrase: After moving through the head bases, breath gives rise to signs such as a pale murky vapor or the skull.

key_passages.anchor: When you have this white light as large as the head, bring it down to The Fifth Base, the center of the chest.
key_passages.paraphrase: Enlarge the white light to head size, then lower it to the chest and spread it through the body.

key_passages.anchor: the ability to see without opening your eyes; the ability to hear far-distant sounds
key_passages.paraphrase: Mastered signs give heightened senses, including seeing with eyes closed.

new_leads: Thanissaro Bhikkhu on nimitta and jhana light
confidence_note: Read in digest only; the seven basic steps and the Method 2 text were not seen, so whether they add induction advice is unconfirmed.
